messages:

Subject: Private deployment – upcoming maintenance window and rollback expectations

Hi Neha / team,

Thanks for the heads up about the July maintenance window. Before we lock dates I need clarity on the following so our security and SRE teams can sign off: 

- Exact downtime impact on inference traffic for pinned Private stacks (session continuity, TCP drains, KV cache invalidation).
- Expected degraded state if rollback is triggered (how does the control plane / data plane behave?).
- Emergency shelve options — can you pin to previous binaries and what is the expected RTO for an undo?

We have a compliance audit in mid-July, so our procurement and security teams want documented rollback criteria and a copy of your runbook that maps roles to commands. Can you attach the runbook and a one-page mutual action plan?

Rita

Hi Rita — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise response and attached the runbook + MAP spreadsheet. High level answers below; detailed playbook is in the PDF.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Impact: planned maintenance is designed to be rolling per-pod with per-tenant pin windows. Typical per-tenant latency impact is negligible (<10ms increase) for short patch cycles; we do *not* expect full traffic interruptions for pinned fleets unless a node eviction is required. We will still surface a short 5–15 minute window where new sessions may get routed to the fallback variant.
- Rollback: we support immediate package shelve to last pinned version (binary + model weights) with an automated KV cache warmback. Our target RTO for a full rollback is 30–90 minutes depending on cache size and sequence length distribution; we list a best-case 30m and worst-case 90m in the runbook.
- Emergency shelve: yes — control plane command "redwood shelve --tenant <id> --version <x.y.z>" documented in runbook. We will request your SRE to run a dry-run with our engineer 48h prior if you want.

Action items I propose: 
1) Joint dry-run (no traffic): Jul 1, 09:00–10:30 UTC — we perform shelve/recover on a staging mirror. 
2) Primary window: Jul 3, 02:00–06:00 UTC — rolling across racks, can be shortened if early success.
3) Communications: pre-window 24h notice, 1h chime, and post-window summary.

Attached: redwood_private_maintenance_runbook_v2.pdf, acme_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Folks — adding a few technical constraints and OKRs from infra side so expectations are aligned. I ran the staging-sim on Wed and noted two failure modes that change the rollback timeline: 

1) KV cache size > 120GB (observed in Acme staging) leads to rewarm times ~45–70m. We can parallelize rewarm across N nodes if you can tolerate transient double-write for 10–15 minutes.
2) Model shard placement: if a shard rebalances during shelve, the streaming clients will observe transient 503s for up to one minute; our guardrail is to stagger shard moves by availability zone.

Proposed mitigations: 
- Limit parallel evictions to 2 racks at a time for your clusters.
- If you enable "fast-warm" (recommended for Acme), we accept a temporary CPU spike during warmback to cut RTO near 25–35 minutes. We flagged this in the runbook under Appendix B.

I also put a quick rollback checklist in the runbook: clear prechecks, traffic-disable flag, shelve command, KV rewarm monitor, and post-restart health probes. Happy to walk ACME SRE through these steps during the dry-run.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Redwood Inference
